This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. After being brought to safety, she was seen sitting in shock, struggling to process the destruction around her. She had survived the dangerous floodwaters, but the disaster had left her facing the painful reality of losing everything she had. The emotional scene reflects the devastating impact of the floods on ordinary families across Nepal. November 14, 2026 Gorkha District, Nepal A large dry landslide occurred in Gorkha District. A mass of earth and rock collapsed from the Gundrung Pakha slope into the Thado Bharyang forest area near Yarubagar. Rocks began falling as early as Friday night, and the main landslide took place around 8:30 a.m., kicking up a massive cloud of dust. Debris reached the Budhi Gandaki River. The landslide blocked both a motorable road and a foot trail. According to the district police, there were no casualties or material damage.
